Sung-Tech Appoints Industry Veteran as Chief Operating Officer Amid Growth Initiatives

SEOUL—Sung-Tech, a leading South Korean technology hardware manufacturer, announced on Monday the appointment of Lee Min-jun as Chief Operating Officer, effective July 1, 2024. The move underscores the company’s commitment to bolstering its operational efficiency and expanding its global footprint amid intensifying competition in the sector.

Lee brings more than 25 years of experience in technology hardware and supply chain management, having previously held senior leadership roles at several prominent East Asian electronics firms. In his new capacity, Lee will oversee Sung-Tech’s global manufacturing operations, supply chain strategy, and new product deployment.

“We are delighted to welcome Mr. Lee to our executive team at a pivotal time for Sung-Tech,” said CEO Park Ji-soo in a statement. “His proven expertise in optimizing large-scale production and navigating complex international supply chains will be invaluable as we continue to pursue innovation-led growth and operational excellence.”

The appointment comes as the South Korean technology hardware industry aims to reinforce its leadership in key global markets. According to the Korea Electronics Manufacturing Association, South Korea accounted for approximately 18% of the world’s semiconductor and device shipments in 2023, with exports valued at $132 billion—a 9% increase over the previous year.

Analysts note that the sector’s rapid growth has prompted firms to invest in talent with deep operational backgrounds. “Companies like Sung-Tech are entering a phase where streamlined operations and agile supply chains are crucial for maintaining competitiveness,” said Ryu Seung-hwan, senior analyst at Daehan Securities. “Bringing in leaders with global manufacturing experience is a logical step as firms look to scale efficiently and respond to shifting demand patterns.”

Industry insiders expect Sung-Tech’s operational initiatives to focus on automation and digital transformation. “The hardware industry is increasingly reliant on smart manufacturing and resilient logistics,” commented Choi Yun-hee, director at the Korea Hardware Technology Forum. “An executive with Lee Min-jun’s background can help drive the adoption of next-generation production systems, which are essential for sustaining export growth.”

Lee expressed optimism about his new role. “I am honored to join Sung-Tech at such an exciting juncture,” he said in a press release. “I look forward to working with the team to enhance our operational capabilities and deliver value to customers worldwide.”

Sung-Tech, which employs more than 6,000 people across its domestic and overseas facilities, recently reported a 14% year-on-year increase in quarterly revenue, citing robust demand for its data storage and connectivity solutions.

Shares of Sung-Tech closed up 1.8% on the Korea Exchange following the announcement.
